board: TGA Islamic Studies scheme (aqeedah, fiqh, seerah, hadith, akhlaq)
source: Adapted from TGA Drive RE/Islamic Studies folder (Al-Baseerah Salah quizzes EYFS-KS1/KS2: gratitude, patience, the Prophet's teaching on salah and the Companions); National Curriculum RE (KS1) | Spring 1 2027 (lessons 1 and 2 upgraded, 13 new): Year 2 pack Islamic Studies Spring 1 weeks 1, 3, 5 (six pillars of iman); hadith of Jibril (Muslim 8); school-approved children's iman books TO CONFIRM | Spring 2 2027 (lessons 5 and 6 upgraded, 14 new): Year 2 pack Islamic Studies Spring 2 weeks 1, 3, 5 (Nuh; Ibrahim; Yunus and Yusuf); ayat 29:14, 19:41, 21:69, 21:87-88, 12:92; no pictures of prophets; lessons v3

lessons.unit: Spring 1: The six pillars of iman
lessons.title: What is iman? Believing in Allah
lessons.bigQuestion: We cannot see the wind, but we know it is there. How?
objectives: To understand that iman means believing in the six pillars, starting with belief in Allah
successCriteria: Most: name the six pillars of iman
Some: say one thing we believe about Allah

keywords.def: believing in our hearts and showing it in what we do
the One who made everything; we worship only Him
to know something is true in your heart
a strong post that holds something up

hook.text: We cannot see the wind, but we know it is there. How?
hook.a: We see what it does: trees move. We cannot see Allah, but we see all He has made.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Say: He is Allah, the One' (al-Ikhlas 112:1).

starter.q: How many pillars of Islam are there?
What is the first pillar of Islam?

teach.heading: What is iman?
bullets: Iman is belief in our hearts
We show iman with good actions
teach.note: Explain that Islam is what we do and iman is what we believe. Angel Jibril asked the Prophet ﷺ about iman and he named six things (Muslim 8). Do not show any picture of an angel.

teach.heading: The six pillars of iman
teach.note: Count them on fingers with the class: one hand plus one.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the poll.

check.q: Which is the FIRST pillar of iman?
check.why: Belief in Allah comes first; all the others come from it.

practice.q: Say the six pillars of iman on your fingers.
practice.a: Allah, angels, books, messengers, Last Day, qadar
practice.model: Thumb: Allah. Pointer: angels. Middle: books. Ring: messengers. Little: Last Day. Other thumb: qadar.

practice.q: Who made the sun, the sea and you?

independent.q: Draw three things Allah made. Write 'Allah made this' under each.
independent.a: For example: the sun, a tree, a cat, each labelled 'Allah made this'.
independent.model: Teacher draws a tree and writes: Allah made this tree.

independent.q: Extend: how many pillars of iman are there?
Stretch: how can we know Allah is there if we cannot see Him?
independent.a: We see everything He made, like we know wind is there when trees move.

exit.q: Back to our ponder: how do we know Allah is there?
exit.a: We see all that He has made.

lessons.homework: Look out of a window with your family and name three things Allah made.
lessons.send: SEND: six-pillar picture card. EAL: repeat 'I believe in Allah'. Stretch: say how iman shows in actions.
resources: Slides
School-approved children's book on iman (TO CONFIRM title with the Islamic Studies lead)
Pupil PDF worksheet: six pillars hand
Colouring pencils

pictures.alt: The night sky, made by Allah

lessons.unit: Spring 1: The six pillars of iman
lessons.title: Belief in the angels and the books
lessons.bigQuestion: If someone wrote down every good word you said today, what would your page say?
objectives: To understand what Muslims believe about Allah's angels and the books He sent
successCriteria: All: say what angels are made from and what they do
Most: name three books Allah sent
Some: say why the Qur'an is special
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: we try to do good because our deeds are written

keywords.def: Allah's helpers made from light who always obey Him
the angel who brought Allah's message to the prophets
Allah's messages sent to prophets
Allah's last book, sent to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ

hook.text: If someone wrote down every good word you said today, what would your page say?
hook.a: Two angels write our good and bad deeds, so we try to fill our page with good.

islamicLink.text: Allah says the Qur'an is protected: 'Indeed, it is We who sent down the message, and indeed, We will be its guardian' (al-Hijr 15:9).

starter.q: How many pillars of iman are there?
What is the first pillar of iman?

teach.heading: Allah's angels
teach.note: Angels were created from light (Muslim, from Aisha). Never draw or show pictures of angels. Name Jibril, who brought the Qur'an. Two angels write what we do (Qur'an 50:17-18).

teach.heading: Allah's books
teach.note: Say each book and the prophet who received it. Pupils repeat.

teach.heading: The Qur'an is special
teach.note: Allah says He will guard the Qur'an (al-Hijr 15:9). Show a mushaf on camera, held respectfully. Ask: how do we treat the Qur'an?

check.q: Which book was sent to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
check.why: The Qur'an. The Zabur came to Dawud and the Tawrah to Musa.

practice.q: Finish: angels are made from ... and they always ... Allah.
practice.model: Angels are made from light. They always obey Allah. They never say no to Him.

independent.q: Match each book to its prophet: Tawrah, Zabur, Injil, Qur'an.
independent.a: Tawrah: Musa; Zabur: Dawud; Injil: Isa; Qur'an: Muhammad ﷺ
independent.model: Teacher draws a line from Qur'an to Muhammad ﷺ and says it aloud.

independent.q: Extend: write one way we show respect to the Qur'an.
independent.a: For example: we keep it clean and high, we make wudu first.

independent.q: Stretch: why do we try to do good if angels write our deeds?
independent.a: So our record is full of good for the Last Day.

exit.q: Back to our ponder: what good word will you add to your page today?
exit.a: For example: thank you, or a kind word to my sister.

lessons.homework: Find the mushaf at home and show your family how we hold and keep it with respect.
lessons.send: SEND: book and prophet matching cards. EAL: repeat book names. Stretch: name two jobs of angels.
resources: Slides
School-approved children's book on iman (TO CONFIRM title with the Islamic Studies lead)
A mushaf shown on camera
Pupil PDF worksheet: books and prophets matching

pictures.alt: A mushaf on a wooden stand
A rehal, a stand to keep the Qur'an high

lessons.unit: Unit 1: The six pillars of iman
lessons.title: Belief in the books
objectives: Name some books Allah revealed
Know the Qur'an is the final book
Know Allah protects the Qur'an

keywords.def: sent down by Allah
the book given to Musa
the book given to Isa

teach.heading: Allah sent books
bullets: Allah sent books to guide people
teach.note: Muslims believe Allah revealed books to messengers: the Tawrah to Musa, the Zabur to Dawud, the Injil to Isa, and the Qur'an to Muhammad ﷺ. Mention Suhuf of Ibrahim. Use respect for other faiths.

teach.heading: The last book
bullets: The Qur'an was sent to Muhammad ﷺ
teach.note: The Qur'an confirms what came before and is the final guidance. Allah protects it. Ask what makes it special: it is Allah's own words.

teach.heading: Protected by Allah
bullets: Allah promised to protect the Qur'an
teach.note: Surah al-Hijr 15:9: indeed We sent down the Reminder and We will guard it. Many Muslims memorise the whole Qur'an. Do not make claims about other books beyond that the Qur'an is guarded by Allah.

teach.heading: Living with the Qur'an
teach.note: Practise respect: clean hands, quiet voice, hold carefully. Ask: how do you show love for the Qur'an this week?

teach.heading: Books chant
teach.note: Match book to messenger. Repeat chant. Highlight the shared message of worshipping Allah alone.

independent: Match the book to the messenger: Tawrah / Zabur / Injil / Qur'an
Write why the Qur'an is special in one sentence
Colour a Qur'an picture and write a manner for it
exit: Which book was given to Muhammad ﷺ?
lessons.homework: Show your family how we hold the Qur'an and tell them what Allah promised.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: matching cards. Stretch: explain why the Qur'an is final.

lessons.title: Prophet Adam: the first human
objectives: Retell the story of Adam
Know Adam was made from clay and taught names
Know Adam asked forgiveness and Allah forgave

keywords.def: wet earth
the one who refused to bow to Adam
to say sorry to Allah and return to Him

starter: Name the angel who brought revelation.

teach.heading: Allah creates Adam
bullets: Allah breathed the soul into him
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Say 'Prophet Adam, alayhis-salam' each time. The Qur'an states that Allah created man from clay (38:71-72). Keep the story to authentic details.

teach.heading: Allah teaches Adam
teach.note: Surah al-Baqarah 2:30-34: angels asked about the vicegerent; Allah taught Adam the names. Angels bowed, Iblis refused out of pride. Draw out: arrogance is a sin. Do not add stories not in the Qur'an or authentic hadith.

teach.heading: The tree
bullets: Adam and his wife lived in Jannah
Allah told them not to eat from one tree
teach.note: Qur'an (7:19-22): they ate; they realised their mistake. Ask: who is our open enemy? Shaytan (2:168). Do not mention the specific tree type or other unauthenticated detail.

teach.heading: Saying sorry
teach.note: Qur'an 7:23: Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves; if You do not forgive us we will be among the losers. Teach the dua in English. Allah accepted Adam's repentance (2:37). Link to our own mistakes.

teach.heading: Lessons
teach.note: Pairs share one lesson. Collect and display. Link to honesty and saying sorry.

practice: What do we do when we make a mistake?
independent: Sequence the story: made from clay / taught names / angels bowed / said sorry
Write: Adam said sorry and Allah ______
Draw a leaf and write one lesson from the story
exit: What did Adam do after the mistake?
lessons.homework: Retell Adam's story to a family member and finish with the dua of Adam.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: story cards in order. Stretch: explain why Iblis refused and why that is wrong.

lessons.title: Prophet Nuh (عليه السلام): obeying Allah and patience
lessons.bigQuestion: Would you keep doing the right thing if everyone laughed at you? Why?
objectives: To understand how Prophet Nuh stayed patient and obeyed Allah
successCriteria: All: retell the story of Nuh in three steps
Most: say how Nuh showed patience
Some: say what the story teaches us about obeying Allah
lessons.smsc: Moral: patience and doing right when it is hard

keywords.def: a man chosen by Allah to bring His message
patience: staying calm and keeping going
the big boat Nuh built
do what Allah tells us

hook.text: Would you keep doing the right thing if everyone laughed at you? Why?
hook.a: Yes, like Nuh: he kept calling people to Allah for many years and stayed patient.

islamicLink.text: Allah tells us about Nuh: he stayed among his people a thousand years less fifty, calling them to Allah (al-'Ankabut 29:14).

starter.q: Bismillah. How many pillars of iman are there?
We believe in Allah's ... (the second pillar)

teach.heading: Nuh calls his people
bullets: Nuh asked his people to worship Allah alone
Most of them refused and laughed
He kept calling for a very long time
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. No pictures of prophets: only objects, places, animals and the sea. The Qur'an says he stayed with them a thousand years less fifty (al-'Ankabut 29:14).

teach.heading: The story in order
teach.note: Pupils hold up 1, 2, 3, 4 fingers as you tell each part.

timeline.text: Allah tells Nuh to build the ark
The flood; the believers and animals are saved

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the poll.

check.q: What did Nuh do when people laughed?
options: He stayed patient and kept going
check.why: Nuh showed sabr: he kept obeying Allah.

practice.q: Retell the story of Nuh in three sentences.
practice.a: Nuh called people to Allah. They laughed. He built the ark and the believers were saved.
practice.model: Teacher: First, Nuh called his people to Allah. Next, they laughed but he stayed patient. Last, Allah saved the believers in the ark.

independent.q: On the pupil PDF story strip, draw the ark and the sea (no people) and write First, Next, Last sentences.
independent.model: Teacher writes 'First, Nuh called his people to worship Allah.'

independent.q: Extend: name two animals that went on the ark.
independent.a: For example: elephants, birds (pairs of animals)

independent.q: Stretch: when do you need to be patient like Nuh?
independent.a: For example: when learning something hard

exit.q: Back to our ponder: would you keep doing right if people laughed?

lessons.homework: Tell the story of Nuh to someone at home using First, Next, Last.
lessons.send: SEND: picture cards to order. EAL: First / Next / Last frame. Stretch: say what 'obey' means with an example.

Pupil PDF worksheet: story strip (ark and sea)
Colouring pencils

lessons.title: Prophet Ibrahim (عليه السلام): trusting Allah and telling the truth
lessons.bigQuestion: Is it easy to tell the truth when everyone around you believes something wrong?
objectives: To understand how Prophet Ibrahim trusted Allah and spoke the truth
successCriteria: All: say why Ibrahim did not worship idols
Most: tell what happened with the fire
Some: say how we can trust Allah too
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: trust in Allah; Moral: courage to tell the truth

keywords.def: trusting Allah
a statue people wrongly worship
saying what is really so
close friend: Ibrahim is the close friend of Allah

hook.text: Is it easy to tell the truth when everyone around you believes something wrong?
hook.a: No, it takes courage. Ibrahim told the truth and trusted Allah.

islamicLink.text: Allah said to the fire: 'O fire, be coolness and safety for Ibrahim' (al-Anbiya 21:69).

teach.heading: Statues cannot help
bullets: People made statues and worshipped them
Ibrahim said they cannot hear or help
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. No pictures of prophets: only objects, places, animals and the sea. Ibrahim was truthful: Allah calls him 'a man of truth, a prophet' (Maryam 19:41).

teach.heading: The fire
bullets: The people threw Ibrahim into a fire
Allah made the fire cool and safe
teach.note: Allah said: 'O fire, be coolness and safety for Ibrahim' (al-Anbiya 21:69). Pause and let pupils feel the wonder.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the poll.

check.q: What did Allah do to the fire?
check.why: Allah protected Ibrahim because he trusted Him (21:69).

practice.q: Why did Ibrahim say the statues were not worth worshipping?
practice.a: They cannot hear, see or help; only Allah can.
practice.model: Teacher: Ibrahim said a statue cannot hear us or help us. Allah hears everything and helps us. So we worship Allah alone.

independent.q: On the pupil PDF, draw flames turning to cool water drops and write: 'Ibrahim trusted Allah, so ...'
independent.model: Teacher writes: Ibrahim trusted Allah, so Allah made the fire cool.

independent.q: Extend: Allah calls Ibrahim His Khalil. What does that mean?
Stretch: give one time you need to tell the truth even if it is hard.
independent.a: For example: owning up after breaking something

exit.q: Back to our ponder: why did Ibrahim tell the truth when it was hard?
exit.a: He trusted Allah and loved the truth.

lessons.homework: Tell a grown-up one true thing you are thankful to Allah for, and the story of the fire.
lessons.send: SEND: three picture cards (statues, fire, cool water). EAL: frame 'Ibrahim trusted Allah, so ...'. Stretch: link 'truth' to Ibrahim's courage.
resources: Slides
Qur'an stories for children from the school's approved list (TO CONFIRM)
Pupil PDF worksheet: fire to coolness
Colouring pencils

lessons.unit: Unit 3: The Prophet's ﷺ mission in Makkah and the Hijrah
lessons.title: Khadijah and the first Muslims
objectives: Name the first Muslims
Know Khadijah supported the Prophet ﷺ
Know early Muslims were patient

keywords.def: the Prophet's first wife and the first to believe
the Prophet's closest friend
the first people to follow Islam

starter: What do we say after the Prophet's name?

teach.heading: Khadijah believes
bullets: Khadijah was the first to believe
She used her wealth for Islam
teach.note: Bismillah. Khadijah bint Khuwaylid, may Allah be pleased with her. Say 'radiyAllahu anha'. She believed when the Prophet ﷺ returned from Hira. Link to the story from Y1.

teach.heading: Friends and family
teach.note: The first men and boys to accept Islam are reported as Abu Bakr, Ali and Zayd. Say 'radiyAllahu anhu'. Highlight that young people believed. Avoid ranking disputes.

teach.heading: Telling others quietly
bullets: At first they called people secretly
teach.note: The first years of the call were private, then public. Keep to this at this level. Explain people were scared but trusted Allah.

teach.heading: What they learned
teach.note: Make a poster of lessons. Ask: what would you have done?

teach.heading: Dua for the Sahabah
bullets: It asks Allah to be pleased with them
teach.note: Teach the phrase. Link to respect for the Companions as part of ahl as-sunnah: we love them and speak well of them. Keep it simple.

practice: Who was the first to believe?
What did Jibril say in Hira?
independent: Match names: Khadijah / Abu Bakr / Ali / Zayd to their descriptions
Write one reason Khadijah was a good supporter
Draw a poster 'Early Muslims were ______'
exit: Who was the first to believe?
lessons.homework: Ask a family member to name a person who helped them be good and thank that person.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: name cards with pictures. Stretch: explain why support matters.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: The Prophet's ﷺ mission in Makkah and the Hijrah
lessons.title: Patience in Makkah: Bilal and the early Muslims
objectives: Know the Muslims were treated badly in Makkah
Know Bilal was freed by Abu Bakr
Learn patience means trusting Allah

keywords.def: being treated unfairly because of beliefs
the Companion who gave the first adhan in Madinah
patience

teach.heading: Hard times
bullets: They did not want idols to be left
teach.note: Say gently: some Muslims were hurt because they would not worship idols. Keep detail light: avoid graphic content. Say Allah rewards patience (39:10: patient ones will be given reward without account).

teach.heading: Bilal
bullets: Abu Bakr bought and freed him
teach.note: This is well-known in the seerah books and is reported by early scholars. Use with care and gentle tone. Bilal later gave the adhan; he said Allahu Akbar. Link to the adhan in Reception.

teach.heading: Sumayyah and Yasir
bullets: Sumayyah was the first woman to give her life for Islam
teach.note: Keep short and reverent. Say radiyAllahu anhum. Avoid any detail beyond the fact that the family was harmed for faith and stayed firm.

teach.heading: What is sabr?
teach.note: The Prophet ﷺ taught that the believer's affair is all good: gratitude when blessed, patience when hurt (Muslim, Suhayb). Say in child words.

teach.heading: Our patience
teach.note: Role-play a short scenario. Praise patient behaviour.

practice: Who was the first to believe?
independent: Write two ways to show patience at school
Match: Bilal / Abu Bakr / Sumayyah to what we remember
Draw an adhan being called and write 'Allahu Akbar'
lessons.homework: Practise sabr this week and tell your family how you did.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: simple timeline of events. Stretch: explain why the early Muslims stayed firm.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: The Prophet's ﷺ mission in Makkah and the Hijrah
lessons.title: The Hijrah: Allah is with us
objectives: Retell the Hijrah simply
Know the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr hid in a cave
Say 'Allah is with us' and mean it

keywords.def: moving from Makkah to Madinah for Allah
the city that welcomed the Muslims
to rely on Allah

starter: Who was freed by Abu Bakr?
Where did the Prophet ﷺ live before Madinah?

teach.heading: Leaving home
bullets: The Quraysh wanted to harm him
Allah told him to go to Madinah
teach.note: Bismillah. The Muslims left Makkah for Madinah. Hijrah means to emigrate for Allah. Say 'sallallahu alayhi wa sallam'. Use a map to show the long journey.

teach.heading: The cave
bullets: The Prophet ﷺ said: Do not grieve, Allah is with us
teach.note: Qur'an 9:40: when they were in the cave he said to his companion, Do not grieve; Allah is with us. Say it slowly. Children repeat. Do not add stories of spiders or doves as authentic facts; some are reported but their authenticity is disputed.

teach.heading: Madinah welcomes
bullets: The people of Madinah welcomed them
The Muslims from Makkah were Muhajirun
teach.note: Introduce Muhajirun and Ansar. Ask: how would you welcome someone new to school? Link to kindness.

teach.heading: Lessons
teach.note: Pairs share. Link to 'Allah is with us' as a comfort in hard times.

teach.heading: Dua of trust
teach.note: Teach: hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakeel (3:173). Explain it means Allah is enough for us and the best one to rely on. Use for difficult moments.

practice: Where was the Prophet ﷺ born?
independent: Sequence the Hijrah: leave Makkah / cave / journey / Madinah
Write: When I am scared I say ______
Draw the cave and write what the Prophet ﷺ said
exit: What did the Prophet ﷺ say in the cave?
Who welcomed the Muslims in Madinah?
lessons.homework: Say 'Hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakeel' when you feel worried and tell someone what it means.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: map and key phrases with pictures. Stretch: explain what the dua means.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: Purity, prayer and good speech
lessons.title: Purity: what breaks wudu
objectives: Remember the steps of wudu
Know some things that break wudu
Know we need wudu for salah

keywords.def: washing parts of the body to pray
makes us need to make wudu again
being clean for worship

starter: What do we say after wudu?

teach.heading: Why wudu?
bullets: The Prophet ﷺ said Allah does not accept prayer without purification
teach.note: The hadith is in Sahih Muslim (Ibn Umar). Say it simply. Also the Prophet ﷺ said sins fall away with the water when a believer makes wudu (Muslim). Keep the tone gentle.

teach.heading: Wudu step review
teach.note: Quick mime of all steps. Check order. Praise correct sequence.

teach.heading: What breaks wudu?
teach.note: At this age keep to the clear ones: anything that exits the private parts, and deep sleep. Say that older classes will learn more. Be matter of fact and respectful; avoid embarrassment.

teach.heading: Staying pure
teach.note: Link to cleanliness being half of faith. Ask: how do you know you need wudu again? Answer using the examples above.

teach.heading: Wudu quiz
teach.note: Show quick scenarios: you ate a sandwich, you used the toilet, you drank water. Children signal thumbs up/down. Correct misconceptions: eating or drinking does not break wudu.

practice: Name the first step of wudu.
What do we say after wudu?
independent: Sort the scenarios: need wudu / do not need wudu
Write the steps of wudu in order (from cards)
Make a numbered wudu chart with labelled steps (words and a water jug, no drawn people)
lessons.homework: Show an adult your wudu steps and ask them to check the order.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: picture cards; sentence frames 'Yes, because ___'. Stretch: explain two reasons wudu is important.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: Purity, prayer and good speech
lessons.title: How to pray: the actions of salah
objectives: Name the actions of salah in order
Know the Prophet ﷺ taught us to pray
Know the words 'Allahu Akbar' and 'Subhana rabbiyal-adheem'

keywords.def: saying Allahu Akbar
bowing
putting the forehead on the ground

teach.heading: Pray as you saw me
bullets: The Prophet ﷺ said: pray as you have seen me pray
We learn by watching and copying
teach.note: Bukhari (Malik ibn al-Huwayrith). Say it in English and Arabic: sallu kama ra'aytumuni usalli. Link to learning from a teacher.

teach.heading: Standing
teach.note: Show the Qiblah direction. Hands: follow the school's madhhab or family custom; do not argue. Fatihah is recited in every rak'ah (Bukhari and Muslim).

teach.heading: Bowing and standing
teach.note: Teach the sayings with actions. The first means Glory to my Lord the Mighty. The second: Allah hears the one who praises Him. The Prophet ﷺ is reported to say them.

teach.heading: Sujood and sitting
teach.note: Subhana rabbiyal-a'la: Glory to my Lord the Most High. The Prophet ﷺ said the closest a servant is to his Lord is in sujood, so make plenty of dua (Muslim). Show how to sit and give salam to right and left.

teach.heading: Practice time
teach.note: Children demonstrate on camera. Praise attention to calm movements. Gentle correction for rushing.

practice: What do we say at the start?
independent: Number the salah actions in order (cards)
Write what we say in ruku and sujood
Teach a partner the actions
exit: What do we say when we bow?
How do we finish the prayer?
lessons.homework: Pray one salah with an adult and practise the words you learned.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: action cards and slow demo; choose a seated option if needed. Stretch: explain the meaning of the dhikr.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: Purity, prayer and good speech
lessons.title: Speak good or be silent
objectives: Know the hadith about good speech
Choose kind words
Avoid unkind words

keywords.def: gentle, true and helpful
saying nothing when words would hurt
polite behaviour

starter: What do we say when we meet?

teach.heading: The hadith
bullets: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day
should speak good or keep silent
teach.note: Read the hadith: whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or be silent. Ask: what is good speech? Gather examples.

teach.heading: Kind words
teach.note: Role-play. Reinforce that Muslims speak gently. Link to Reception and Year 1 manners.

teach.heading: Unkind words
teach.note: The Qur'an says do not mock others; they may be better than you (49:11). Keep the example age-appropriate. Ask how name-calling feels.

teach.heading: When to be silent
bullets: When you have nothing good to say
teach.note: Teach the pause: breathe, say Audhu billahi mina ash-shaytan ir-rajeem if angry. The strong person controls himself when angry (Bukhari and Muslim).

teach.heading: Word tally
teach.note: Give each child a mini tally to use during the week. Praise sharing.

practice: Give an example of a kind thing.
independent: Sort statements into kind / unkind
Rewrite an unkind sentence as a kind one (3 examples)
Role-play saying sorry with a partner
exit: What does the hadith tell us to do?
Give one kind thing to say.
lessons.homework: Count how many kind words you say at home today and tell us.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: sentence cards with kind starters. Stretch: explain why silence can be good.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: The six pillars of iman
lessons.title: Belief in the messengers, the Last Day and qadar
lessons.bigQuestion: If it rains on the day of your picnic, is that bad luck, or something else?
objectives: To understand what Muslims believe about Allah's messengers, the Last Day and qadar
successCriteria: Most: say what happens on the Last Day in one sentence
Some: explain qadar as Allah's plan with trust and effort
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: trust in Allah when plans change

keywords.def: a person Allah chose to teach people His message
the day everyone will stand before Allah
Allah knows and plans everything
if Allah wills

hook.text: If it rains on the day of your picnic, is that bad luck, or something else?
hook.a: Allah knows best; we say alhamdulillah and make a new plan. That is belief in qadar.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it' (az-Zalzalah 99:7).

starter.q: Which book came to Prophet Musa?

teach.heading: Allah's messengers
bullets: Allah sent messengers to every people
teach.note: Name Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa and Muhammad ﷺ (peace be upon them). Say ﷺ after the Prophet's name. No pictures of prophets.

teach.heading: The Last Day
bullets: One day this world will end
teach.note: Keep it gentle and hopeful: Allah is fair and merciful. Every small good deed counts (az-Zalzalah 99:7).

teach.heading: Qadar: Allah's plan
bullets: Allah knows everything before it happens
teach.note: Use the picnic story: we plan, we pray, and we accept what Allah decides.

check.q: It rains on your picnic day. What should a Muslim do?
options: Say alhamdulillah and make a new plan
check.why: Belief in qadar means trusting Allah's plan and trying again.

practice.q: Say all six pillars of iman.
practice.a: Allah, angels, books, messengers, Last Day, qadar
practice.model: I count on my fingers: Allah, angels, books, messengers, the Last Day, qadar.

independent.q: Write one sentence for each: messengers, Last Day, qadar.
independent.a: For example: Allah sent messengers to teach us. On the Last Day we stand before Allah. Qadar means Allah has a plan.
independent.model: Teacher writes: Allah sent messengers to teach people to worship Him.

independent.q: Stretch: why do we say in sha Allah when we plan?
independent.a: Because only Allah knows what will happen.

exit.q: Back to our ponder: rain on picnic day is ...
exit.a: Part of Allah's plan; we say alhamdulillah and try again.

lessons.homework: Say all six pillars of iman to someone at home and tell them one sentence about each.
lessons.send: SEND: six-pillar picture card. EAL: model 'I believe in ...'. Stretch: explain how believing in the Last Day helps us be good.

lessons.title: Prophets Yunus and Yusuf (عليهما السلام): hope and forgiveness
lessons.bigQuestion: Have you ever forgiven someone who was unkind to you? How did it feel?
objectives: To understand how Yunus kept hope in Allah and how Yusuf forgave his brothers
successCriteria: All: retell one story in order
Most: say the lesson of each story
Some: say Yunus's du'a and when we could use it
lessons.smsc: Moral: forgiveness; Spiritual: hope in Allah

keywords.def: believing Allah will help
letting go of being upset with someone
asking Allah
a huge sea animal

hook.text: Have you ever forgiven someone who was unkind to you? How did it feel?
hook.a: Forgiving feels light and Allah loves it, like Yusuf with his brothers.

islamicLink.text: Yunus called out in the darkness: 'There is no god but You, glory be to You; I have been one of the wrongdoers', and Allah saved him (al-Anbiya 21:87-88).

starter.q: Bismillah. Allah made the fire cool for ...

teach.heading: Yunus in the whale
bullets: Yunus left his people without waiting
He was swallowed by a whale
In the dark he made du'a; Allah saved him
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. No pictures of prophets: only objects, places, animals and the sea. Read the du'a slowly: 'There is no god but You, glory be to You; I have been one of the wrongdoers' (al-Anbiya 21:87).

teach.heading: Yusuf forgives
bullets: His brothers threw him in a well
Years later he became a leader in Egypt
He forgave them: 'No blame on you today'
teach.note: Yusuf said: 'No blame will there be upon you today' (Yusuf 12:92). Ask: why is forgiving strong, not weak?

teach.heading: Two stories, two lessons
teach.note: Read each card; pupils show 1 or 2.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the poll.

check.q: What did Yunus do inside the whale?
check.why: He made du'a and kept hope; Allah saved him.

practice.q: Tell Yunus's story in three steps.
practice.a: He left, was swallowed by the whale, made du'a and was saved.
practice.model: Teacher: First, Yunus left his people. Next, a whale swallowed him and he made du'a. Last, Allah saved him.

independent.q: On the pupil PDF, draw a whale and a well (no people). Write one lesson under each.
independent.a: Whale: never lose hope; well: forgive others.
independent.model: Teacher writes under the whale: Never lose hope; make du'a.

independent.q: Extend: say the start of Yunus's du'a: 'La ilaha illa anta ...'
independent.a: La ilaha illa anta subhanaka (There is no god but You, glory be to You)

independent.q: Stretch: when could you say Yunus's du'a?
independent.a: When something is hard or I have done wrong

exit.q: Back to our ponder: how does forgiving feel?
exit.a: Light and good; Allah loves those who forgive.

lessons.homework: Retell one of today's stories at home in order, with its lesson. (This is your story check for the half term.)
lessons.send: SEND: four picture cards to sort. EAL: frame 'The lesson is ...'. Stretch: compare how Nuh, Ibrahim and Yunus each trusted Allah.
